buildIssueRecordAuthorizationData.reason: Legacy single-issue writes (issue #244) authorize against LegacyIssueWriteAuthorization: the viewer projection of the workspace, team and viewer policy plus only the projects and cycles the body names, then the same issue and ancestor query. Legacy comment-action reads use scoped viewer and team policy with the same query. The remaining legacy complete projections (issue creation, batch, release edits, reads, bodies naming further issues, and stores without an installed workspace) are charged to the shared projection gate before they are built. Bounded child, permission and comment-action routes retain their proven reader. The remaining bounded routes use boundedIssueRecordAuthorizationMetadata and own the issue headers, first-page ancestors, comment author and authorization inputs until output. TestIssueWriteDifferential compares scoped and complete reads for 25 routes x 9 principals x 5 issue shapes in legacy, hydrated and bounded-view modes; TestIssueWriteAllocations measures allocation as unrelated projects and histories grow. TestIssueRecordAuthorizationDifferential compares legacy/warm/reloaded authorization decisions and exact consumed headers for 24 route/input cases x 20 M principals/credentials (960 pairs).
buildIssueRecordAuthorizationData.temperatureReason: Issue alias authorization and handoff shared by comment/reaction/create/update routes.

completeIssueRecordProjection.reason: A handler on a scoped legacy single-issue write that still reads workspaceData gets the projection it read before: the viewer's complete projection with the authorized issue rows and comment, built once on first read under the shared projection gate. The issue #244 differential compares both paths.
completeIssueRecordProjection.temperatureReason: Only handlers that read workspaceData after a scoped issue write authorization, such as the issue permission routes.
